situation:
You are the promotions manager at COURTLAND ATHLETIC CLUBS, a chain of eleven fitness and racquet clubs. The founder (judge), who opened the first club close to twenty-five years ago, is preparing to hand the business to a buyer at the end of the year, and has asked you to recommend how the clubs' Open Courts Weekend will be staffed.

Open Courts Weekend is the chain's largest promotional event and the weekend when most of the year's new memberships are sold. Members bring guests, the clubs run free clinics, the cafe serves all day, and the courts stay busy from early morning until closing. It is also the last one the founder (judge) will run, and every promise made around it will be inherited by the buyer.

Two signed agreements now point at the same court-side demonstration stations. The clubs' part-time staff work under a scheduling agreement that gives them first claim on all event hours, and those hours are the largest paycheck many of them earn all year. PALISADE RACQUET, the weekend's title sponsor, signed a sponsorship contract requiring its own certified demonstration staff to run the demonstration stations.

Assigning the demonstration stations to the certified staff from PALISADE RACQUET protects the sponsorship money that pays for the weekend, and it takes roughly sixty promised event hours away from the part-time staff and breaks the scheduling agreement they were given in writing. Keeping the demonstration stations for the part-time staff honors that agreement, and it puts the sponsorship renewal at risk and leaves the weekend without the funding the sponsor supplies.

The founder (judge) wants your recommendation on which agreement the clubs will honor, how the core values of the membership experience should be communicated to the guests the weekend is meant to reach, and what the clubs owe the people the decision costs. The founder (judge) will greet you, hear your ideas and ask questions. When you have finished answering, the founder (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are to assume the role of founder (judge) of COURTLAND ATHLETIC CLUBS, a chain of eleven fitness and racquet clubs.

Business background is the same as the situation above. You are handing the business to a buyer at the end of the year. The part-time staff hold a scheduling agreement giving them first claim on all event hours, and the sponsorship contract with PALISADE RACQUET requires the sponsor's own certified demonstration staff at the court-side stations. Both agreements cover the same weekend.

You have asked the promotions manager (participant) to recommend which agreement the clubs honor, how the core values of the membership experience reach guests during Open Courts Weekend, and what the clubs owe the people the decision costs.

During the course of the role-play you are to ask the participant the following questions:
judgeQuestions: Who does this decision cost the most, and how would you tell them?
What should the part-time staff hear from us about next year's Open Courts Weekend?
